description: Embedded systems + IoT + real-time as graph-resident theory. Critical to the agent's eventual embodied form: tight sensorimotor loops, resource constraints, determinism guarantees, fault tolerance. Beyond what operating_systems covered (scheduling, sync primitives) and computer_architecture (caches, pipelines): hard/soft/firm real-time, WCET, RT schedulability (RMS, EDF, DM), RTOSes (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, VxWorks, QNX, PREEMPT_RT), microcontrollers (Cortex-M, RISC-V, ESP32, STM32), bare-metal programming (memory-mapped IO, DMA, registers), interrupt handling, power management, peripherals (I2C, SPI, UART, ADC, DAC, PWM), IoT protocols (MQTT, CoAP, BLE, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, LoRaWAN, NB-IoT), real-time communication (TSN, CAN, EtherCAT, OPC UA, DDS), robotics middleware (ROS2, micro-ROS), sensor fusion (Kalman, particle filters), embedded ML (TinyML, TFLite Micro), safety-critical (DO-178C, ISO 26262, ASIL, MISRA C), fault tolerance (TMR, lockstep, watchdog). The constraints that determine what an embodied agent can actually do.
category_inheritance: genlMt → compiler_theory + operating_systems + computer_architecture + network_protocols. Determinism guarantees map directly to compiler_theory equivalence vocabulary: WCET = cost equivalence with bounds; real-time correctness = referential transparency (output depends only on input + bounded time, not on other factors); safety-critical guarantees = denotational equivalence under all input conditions.

concepts.name: hard_realtime
concepts.definition: Missing a deadline = system failure. Pacemaker, airbag, flight control, ABS brakes.
concepts.why: Safety-critical. Late = wrong. Worst-case must be guaranteed. Cannot be a probabilistic system — every deadline always met. Foundation of safety-critical embedded.

concepts.name: soft_realtime
concepts.definition: Missing deadlines degrades quality but not safety. Video frame drops, audio glitches, game frame rate.
concepts.why: Best-effort timing. Occasional misses acceptable. Most consumer real-time systems. Different correctness criterion than hard RT.

concepts.name: firm_realtime
concepts.definition: Late results have zero value but no safety consequences. Stock trading, video conferencing late frames.
concepts.why: Late = dropped, not used. Between hard + soft. Some occasional misses tolerable but lateness yields no benefit.

concepts.name: determinism
concepts.definition: Same input + same state → same output + same timing. Predictable behaviour.
concepts.why: Foundation of RT analysis. Non-determinism (caches, branch prediction, DRAM refresh) hurts RT predictability. Critical for safety.

concepts.name: worst_case_execution_time
concepts.definition: WCET: maximum possible execution time of a code path. Computed via static analysis or measured.
concepts.why: RT scheduling assumes WCETs. Tight bound → tight schedule. Loose bound → wasted CPU. WCET analysis is its own field.

concepts.name: jitter
concepts.definition: Variation in latency between events. Caused by interrupts, cache misses, GC pauses, scheduler decisions.
concepts.why: RT systems care about both mean + worst-case + jitter. Audio: low jitter for synchronisation. Control loops: jitter affects stability.

concepts.name: latency_RT
concepts.definition: Time from event to response. Interrupt latency, scheduling latency, communication latency.
concepts.why: RT system end-to-end metric. Stack: HW latency + ISR + OS schedule + task execution + output. Each layer contributes; all must be bounded.

concepts.name: FreeRTOS
concepts.definition: Open-source RTOS. Tiny (~10 KB). Preemptive priority scheduling + cooperative. Used in millions of devices.
concepts.why: De facto MCU RTOS. AWS-stewarded since 2017. Tasks, queues, semaphores, mutexes, software timers. Standard for ARM Cortex-M projects.

concepts.name: Zephyr
concepts.definition: Linux Foundation RTOS. POSIX-like API, scalable from 8-bit to 64-bit. Strong network + Bluetooth stacks.
concepts.why: Modern open RTOS. Better networking + drivers than FreeRTOS. Increasing adoption (Nordic, Intel, NXP backed).

concepts.name: VxWorks
concepts.definition: Commercial RTOS. Wind River. Used in Mars rovers, Boeing 787, industrial control.
concepts.why: Aerospace + industrial standard. Hard RT certified for DO-178C. Mature ecosystem; license cost = enterprise.

concepts.name: QNX
concepts.definition: Microkernel RTOS. BlackBerry. Used in cars (CarPlay backend), medical, industrial.
concepts.why: Microkernel architecture: drivers + filesystems in userspace. Fault tolerance via isolation. Automotive standard.

concepts.name: PREEMPT_RT
concepts.definition: Linux kernel patch making it preemptible everywhere. Bounded scheduling latencies.
concepts.why: Linux for RT. Mainlined incrementally since 2004. Real-time Linux for industrial + audio + robotics. Maintained by Linux Foundation Real-Time Linux project.

concepts.name: rate_monotonic_scheduling
concepts.definition: RMS: priority = inverse of period. Higher frequency tasks get higher priority. Optimal for fixed priorities.
concepts.why: Liu + Layland 1973. Provably optimal among fixed-priority schedulers. Schedulability via utilisation bound. Foundation of RT scheduling theory.

concepts.name: earliest_deadline_first
concepts.definition: EDF: task with closest deadline runs next. Dynamic priorities.
concepts.why: Optimal among all schedulers: schedulable iff total utilisation ≤ 1. Cost: priority changes per release. Less used than RMS in practice (harder to analyse).

concepts.name: deadline_monotonic
concepts.definition: DM: priority = inverse of relative deadline. Variant of RMS for tasks with deadline < period.
concepts.why: Generalises RMS. Optimal for fixed priority when deadlines ≤ periods. Used when deadlines aren't tied to release periods.

concepts.name: schedulability_analysis
concepts.definition: Prove that a task set meets all deadlines under given scheduler. Response time analysis (RTA), utilisation bound.
concepts.why: RT system must be proven schedulable. RTA: iteratively compute worst-case response time per task. UB: simpler but conservative.

concepts.name: priority_inheritance_RT
concepts.definition: Already in OS Mt. Critical in RT: low-priority task holding mutex inherits high-priority task's priority. Prevents unbounded priority inversion.
concepts.why: Mars Pathfinder famous bug (1997): priority inversion crashed rover. Fix: priority inheritance. Standard RT primitive.

concepts.name: priority_ceiling_protocol
concepts.definition: Mutex has ceiling = max priority of any task using it. Task holding mutex runs at ceiling.

b.value: max priority of any task using it

concepts.why: Prevents deadlock + bounded priority inversion. More predictable than priority inheritance. Used in safety-critical RT.

concepts.name: rate_monotonic_utilisation_bound
concepts.definition: U_max(n) = n × (2^(1/n) - 1). For n tasks, set schedulable if utilisation ≤ this bound. Converges to ln(2) ≈ 0.693.
concepts.why: Quick schedulability check. Sufficient but not necessary. RTA gives tight bound; UB is conservative.

concepts.name: interrupt_service_routine
concepts.definition: ISR: function called by hardware interrupt. Runs in interrupt context (can't sleep, restricted API).
concepts.why: Hardware async events handled here. Keep short: just acknowledge + signal task. Long ISRs delay other interrupts.

concepts.name: interrupt_latency
concepts.definition: Time from interrupt assertion to first ISR instruction. Hardware + (current critical section).
concepts.why: Critical RT metric. Cortex-M3+ has ~12 cycle deterministic interrupt entry. Disabling interrupts adds to worst case.

concepts.name: interrupt_top_bottom_half
concepts.definition: Top half (ISR): minimal, acknowledge hardware. Bottom half (deferred): heavy processing.
concepts.why: Linux convention. ISR enables interrupts quickly; tasklet/workqueue does the work. Pattern in all RT-aware systems.

concepts.name: nested_vectored_interrupt_controller
concepts.definition: NVIC: Cortex-M interrupt controller. Hardware-prioritised, nested interrupts, tail-chaining.
concepts.why: Deterministic interrupt entry. Tail-chaining: back-to-back interrupts skip stack save/restore. Hardware advantage of Cortex-M.

concepts.name: ARM_Cortex_M
concepts.definition: 32-bit MCU family. M0 (low power, basic), M3 (general), M4F (DSP + FPU), M7 (performance), M33 (security TrustZone).
concepts.why: Dominant 32-bit MCU. STM32, nRF, MKL, RP2040 all Cortex-M. Standard instruction set (ARMv7-M, v8-M). Well-supported tooling.

concepts.name: RISC_V_embedded
concepts.definition: Open ISA. RV32E (embedded, 16 registers), RV32I (full), with optional extensions.
concepts.why: No license fees. ESP32-C3, GD32V, BL602, Bouffalo, Alibaba T-Head. Growing market share. Modular ISA fits embedded.

concepts.name: ESP32
concepts.definition: Espressif. Xtensa or RISC-V cores. Wi-Fi + Bluetooth integrated. Cheap (<$5).
concepts.why: IoT workhorse. Wide community. Trade: large for what it is (256 KB SRAM typical), power-hungry vs pure Cortex-M.

concepts.name: STM32
concepts.definition: ST Microelectronics Cortex-M family. Vast peripherals + variants.
concepts.why: Most popular Cortex-M family. Comprehensive HAL + IDE (STM32Cube). Industry standard for ARM MCUs.

concepts.name: AVR_8_bit
concepts.definition: Atmel/Microchip 8-bit. Arduino UNO is ATmega328. Simple, well-understood.
concepts.why: Education + hobby. Slower + smaller than ARM but lower complexity. Legacy + entry-level products.

concepts.name: RP2040
concepts.definition: Raspberry Pi Foundation. Dual Cortex-M0+, PIO (Programmable IO).
concepts.why: Modern hobby + commercial. PIO is unique: state machines for custom bit-banging at hardware speed. Used in many products.

concepts.name: memory_mapped_IO
concepts.definition: Hardware peripheral registers appear as memory addresses. Read/write to address = control hardware.
concepts.why: Foundation of bare-metal. No special instruction; just pointer access. volatile keyword critical (compiler must not optimise).

concepts.name: DMA_controller
concepts.definition: Direct Memory Access. Peripheral ↔ memory transfer without CPU.
concepts.why: Critical for performance + RT. CPU free for other work. DMA: setup once, transfer many. Standard for fast peripherals (SPI, I2S, ADC).

concepts.name: bootloader
concepts.definition: Initial code that loads main application. Verifies + may update firmware.
concepts.why: Foundation of safe firmware update. Bootloader is rarely updated; application can be. Patterns: A/B partitions, rollback on failure.

concepts.name: watchdog_timer
concepts.definition: Hardware timer; resets MCU if not periodically 'kicked'. Forces reset on hang.
concepts.why: Last-resort recovery. Task stuck → no kick → reset → recover. Critical for unattended embedded.

concepts.name: linker_script
concepts.definition: Maps program sections to memory regions. .text → FLASH, .data → RAM init, .bss → RAM zero.
concepts.why: Embedded needs explicit memory layout. Reserved regions for bootloader, application, EEPROM emulation. Different from desktop linkers.

concepts.name: GPIO
concepts.definition: General Purpose Input/Output. Digital pins, configurable direction + pull-up/down.
concepts.why: Most basic peripheral. LED, button, custom signalling. Foundation of physical world interaction. Atomic register access matters.

concepts.name: I2C
concepts.definition: Two-wire serial bus. Multi-master, addressable slaves. Speed up to 5 MHz.
concepts.why: Standard for sensors, EEPROMs, displays. 7-bit address space. Bidirectional. Pull-up resistors required.

concepts.name: SPI
concepts.definition: Synchronous serial bus. 4 wires: CLK, MOSI, MISO, CS. Faster than I2C (10+ MHz).
concepts.why: Storage (flash), displays, fast sensors. Full-duplex. Multiple slaves via separate CS lines. No addressing.

concepts.name: UART
concepts.definition: Universal Async Receiver/Transmitter. 2 wires + ground. No clock; configurable baud rate.
concepts.why: Console + GPS + GSM modules. Simplest serial. Hardware FIFOs reduce CPU load. Common debug interface.

concepts.name: ADC_resolution
concepts.definition: Analog-to-Digital Converter. 8 to 24 bit. Sampling rate kHz to MHz.
concepts.why: Read analog sensors (voltage, current, temperature). Resolution + reference voltage determine accuracy. Standard MCU peripheral.

concepts.name: DAC
concepts.definition: Digital-to-Analog Converter. Outputs analog voltage.
concepts.why: Audio, analog control signals. PWM often substitutes for DAC. True DAC for precise analog output.

concepts.name: PWM
concepts.definition: Pulse Width Modulation. Variable duty cycle digital signal.
concepts.why: Motor speed control, LED brightness, fake DAC. Simple + powerful. Hardware timers generate. ESC for motors uses PWM.

concepts.name: static_memory_allocation
concepts.definition: All memory determined at compile time. No malloc/free.
concepts.why: Required in hard RT + safety-critical. No fragmentation, predictable. Worst-case memory usage knowable. MISRA C forbids dynamic alloc.

concepts.name: memory_pool
concepts.definition: Pre-allocated array of fixed-size blocks. Allocate from pool, return to pool.
concepts.why: Bounded allocation time. No fragmentation. Standard pattern when need dynamic-like alloc with RT bounds.

concepts.name: stack_overflow_protection
concepts.definition: Detect stack overflow via guard word, MMU/MPU, or canary. Trigger reset before corruption.
concepts.why: Embedded stacks tiny (KB). Recursion + deep call chains = overflow = corruption = mysterious crash. MPU regions catch.

concepts.name: memory_protection_unit
concepts.definition: MPU: simpler than MMU. Permission regions, no virtual memory.
concepts.why: Cortex-M has MPU not MMU. Protect kernel from app, app from itself. Required for some safety certifications.

concepts.name: low_power_modes
concepts.definition: Sleep, deep sleep, stop, standby. CPU off, RAM retained or off, peripherals selectively on.
concepts.why: Battery + energy-harvesting devices. Sleep majority of time; wake on event. nRF52: μA in deep sleep.

concepts.name: wake_on_interrupt
concepts.definition: MCU sleeps; peripheral interrupt wakes. Common: timer, GPIO, communication.
concepts.why: Event-driven low power. Wake → process → sleep. Average current = peak × duty cycle. Foundation of energy-constrained design.

concepts.name: energy_harvesting
concepts.definition: Solar, vibration, thermal, RF. Generate microwatts. Buffer + use when threshold met.
concepts.why: Self-powered IoT. No batteries to replace. Trade: very limited compute budget (microjoules per operation).

concepts.name: MQTT_pubsub
concepts.definition: Publish-subscribe over TCP. Broker-based. Topics with hierarchy. QoS 0/1/2.
concepts.why: IoT messaging standard. Lightweight (compared to HTTP). Used in Home Assistant, AWS IoT Core, many products. RFC 3.1.1 + v5.

concepts.name: MQTT_QoS_levels
concepts.definition: QoS 0: at-most-once. QoS 1: at-least-once. QoS 2: exactly-once.
concepts.why: Application controls reliability. QoS 2 expensive (4-way handshake). QoS 1 common default.

concepts.name: CoAP
concepts.definition: Constrained Application Protocol. RESTful over UDP. RFC 7252.
concepts.why: Like HTTP but tiny. Multicast support. Resource discovery. Designed for constrained devices + 6LoWPAN networks.

concepts.name: LwM2M
concepts.definition: Lightweight M2M. Device management protocol on CoAP. OMA standard.
concepts.why: Standard IoT device management: register, query, control, firmware update. Used heavily in cellular IoT (NB-IoT, LTE-M).

concepts.name: BLE_GATT
concepts.definition: Bluetooth Low Energy Generic Attribute Profile. Services + characteristics. Low-power radio.
concepts.why: Wearables, smart home, beacons. ~5 mW peak. iOS + Android native support. Mesh, Audio extensions.

concepts.name: Zigbee
concepts.definition: IEEE 802.15.4-based mesh networking. 2.4 GHz. Low power.
concepts.why: Smart home (Hue, Ikea, SmartThings). Mesh extends range. Self-healing. Largely superseded by Thread + Matter.

concepts.name: Thread
concepts.definition: IPv6-based mesh on 802.15.4. Designed for home IoT. Connected Home Alliance.
concepts.why: Foundation of Matter. IPv6 native. Self-healing mesh. Border routers bridge to IP networks. Modern Zigbee successor.

concepts.name: Matter
concepts.definition: Smart home standard. CHIP (Connected Home over IP). Runs over Thread + Wi-Fi. Connectivity Standards Alliance.
concepts.why: Apple, Google, Amazon, Samsung consortium. Unified smart home. Vendor-agnostic. Industry consolidation move.

concepts.name: 6LoWPAN
concepts.definition: IPv6 over Low-Power Wireless Personal Area Networks. Header compression for 802.15.4.
concepts.why: Foundation: IP networks reaching tiny devices. Header compression critical (IPv6 = 40 bytes; 802.15.4 frame = 127 bytes). Used in Thread.

concepts.name: LoRaWAN
concepts.definition: Long Range WAN. Sub-GHz, license-free ISM bands. km range, ~1 kbps.
concepts.why: Wide-area low-power. Battery years. Cost: low throughput, often gateway-dependent. Used for sensors, asset tracking.

concepts.name: NB_IoT_LTE_M
concepts.definition: Cellular IoT. NB-IoT: ultra-low data, deep coverage. LTE-M: higher data, mobility.
concepts.why: Cellular operators offer. Global coverage. Cost: SIM, subscription. Used for asset tracking, smart meters, agriculture.

concepts.name: Sigfox
concepts.definition: Proprietary LPWAN. Tiny messages (12 bytes), 140/day uplink. Free-ish.
concepts.why: Pure low-data use cases. Network operator-led. Coverage limited; declining vs LoRaWAN.

concepts.name: CAN_bus
concepts.definition: Controller Area Network. Differential pair, message-based, arbitration via ID priority.
concepts.why: Automotive standard. 1 Mbps classic, 5 Mbps CAN FD. Deterministic message delivery. Used in robotics, industrial too.

concepts.name: LIN_bus
concepts.definition: Local Interconnect Network. Single-wire, master-slave. Cheaper than CAN.
concepts.why: Automotive: window switches, sensors. Slower (20 kbps). CAN where speed needed; LIN where cost.

concepts.name: FlexRay
concepts.definition: Automotive bus. Time-triggered + event-triggered. 10 Mbps.
concepts.why: X-by-wire (drive-by-wire, brake-by-wire). Deterministic timing. Used in safety-critical automotive. Increasingly displaced by Ethernet.

concepts.name: Time_Sensitive_Networking_TSN
concepts.definition: IEEE 802.1 standards adding determinism to Ethernet. Time-aware shaping, frame preemption, redundancy.
concepts.why: Standard Ethernet + determinism. Industrial automation, automotive, professional audio. Modern alternative to specialised RT buses.

concepts.name: EtherCAT
concepts.definition: Industrial Ethernet protocol. On-the-fly processing — slaves modify packet as it passes.
concepts.why: Microsecond-level industrial control. Beckhoff. Common in motion control, robotics. Determinism + speed.

concepts.name: PROFINET
concepts.definition: Industrial Ethernet by Siemens. Various profiles (basic to ultra-low latency).
concepts.why: Industrial automation. Real-time variants. Largest deployed industrial Ethernet.

concepts.name: OPC_UA
concepts.definition: Open Platform Communications - Unified Architecture. Industrial M2M. Built-in security + info model.
concepts.why: Industry 4.0 / IIoT data layer. Vendor-neutral. Server-client + pub/sub. Standard for industrial integration.

concepts.name: DDS_data_distribution
concepts.definition: Data Distribution Service. Real-time pub/sub. Decentralised. QoS-rich.
concepts.why: Foundation of ROS2. Used in defense, aerospace, industrial. RTI Connext, eProsima Fast DDS, OpenDDS. Strong typing + discovery.

concepts.name: ROS2
concepts.definition: Robot Operating System v2. Nodes + topics + services + actions + parameters. Over DDS.
concepts.why: Standard robotics middleware. Distributed: nodes communicate via DDS. Versus ROS1: real-time-capable, multi-platform. Industry direction.

concepts.name: micro_ROS
concepts.definition: ROS2 for microcontrollers. Client library runs on MCU; agent bridges to ROS2 network.
concepts.why: Microcontroller can be a ROS2 node. Use cases: sensors, actuators with rich semantics. Cortex-M3+ minimum.

concepts.name: ROS2_QoS_profiles
concepts.definition: Per-topic QoS: history, reliability, durability, deadline, liveliness, latency budget.
concepts.why: Fine-grained reliability. Best-effort for sensor streams; reliable for commands. Tunable per requirements.

concepts.name: URDF_robot_description
concepts.definition: Unified Robot Description Format. XML describing robot's links + joints + kinematics.
concepts.why: Standard robotics model format. Used by ROS for visualisation, planning, simulation. URDF + meshes describe physical robot.

concepts.name: IMU
concepts.definition: Inertial Measurement Unit. Accelerometer + gyroscope (+ magnetometer = 9-DOF).
concepts.why: Foundation of motion sensing. Drones, robots, AR/VR, fitness. Bias drift over time = fusion required.

concepts.name: LIDAR
concepts.definition: Light Detection and Ranging. Pulsed laser distance. 2D or 3D point clouds.
concepts.why: Autonomous vehicles, mapping, robotics. mm precision. Cost: expensive (declining). Solid-state vs mechanical scanning.

concepts.name: time_of_flight_sensor
concepts.definition: ToF: measures distance via light reflection time. mm-cm resolution.
concepts.why: Phone cameras (portrait mode), robot proximity, gesture recognition. Cheaper than LIDAR; limited range (few meters).

concepts.name: rotary_encoder
concepts.definition: Sensor measuring shaft rotation. Incremental (counts) or absolute (knows position).
concepts.why: Motor feedback, robotic joints. Quadrature: 2 signals 90° offset = direction + position. Foundation of closed-loop motor control.

concepts.name: event_camera
concepts.definition: Pixel-level async sensor. Each pixel reports brightness change events.
concepts.why: Microsecond temporal resolution, low power, sparse data. Different paradigm vs frame cameras. Used in fast robotics, neuromorphic.

concepts.name: BLDC_motor
concepts.definition: Brushless DC motor. Electronic commutation via ESC. High efficiency + power density.
concepts.why: Drones, e-bikes, modern robotics. ESCs (Electronic Speed Controllers) drive. Requires position feedback (sensored) or back-EMF (sensorless).

concepts.name: servo_motor
concepts.definition: Motor with built-in position feedback + control. Move to specified angle.
concepts.why: Hobby robotics, RC. PWM controlled. Simple to use. Limited torque + speed; not for high power.

concepts.name: stepper_motor
concepts.definition: Motor that moves in fixed angular steps. Open-loop position control possible.
concepts.why: 3D printers, CNC, precise positioning. No feedback needed (if not lost steps). Higher torque at low speed than servo.

concepts.name: Kalman_filter
concepts.definition: Recursive state estimator. Combines prediction + measurement weighted by uncertainty.
concepts.why: Sensor fusion foundation. IMU + GPS, vision + IMU. Optimal for Gaussian-linear systems. Extended (EKF) + Unscented (UKF) for non-linear.

concepts.name: complementary_filter
concepts.definition: Simple sensor fusion: weighted sum of high-pass + low-pass filtered signals.
concepts.why: Cheaper than Kalman. IMU attitude: low-pass accelerometer + high-pass gyro integration. Good enough for many applications.

concepts.name: particle_filter
concepts.definition: Monte Carlo state estimation. Many sample states; resampled based on observations.
concepts.why: Non-linear, non-Gaussian. Localization (Monte Carlo Localization in robotics). Cost: many particles.

concepts.name: TinyML
concepts.definition: Machine learning on MCUs (kB RAM). TensorFlow Lite Micro, edge-impulse, MicroTVM.
concepts.why: Inference at extreme edge. Wake word detection, anomaly detection, gesture recognition. Quantised models, fixed-point math.

concepts.name: TFLite_Micro
concepts.definition: TF Lite for Microcontrollers. Few-KB runtime. No allocator (static memory).
concepts.why: Standard for MCU ML. Supports Cortex-M, ESP32, etc. Kernels optimised per platform. CMSIS-NN underneath on ARM.

concepts.name: ML_quantization_embedded
concepts.definition: Float32 weights → int8 (or int4). 4-8x smaller. Hardware-friendly (no FPU needed).
concepts.why: Critical for embedded. Cortex-M0/M3 have no FPU. Int8 inference much faster + smaller. Cost: ~1-2% accuracy.

concepts.name: DO_178C_avionics
concepts.definition: Software considerations in airborne systems. DALs (Design Assurance Levels) A-E.
concepts.why: FAA-mandated for avionics. Level A (catastrophic failure) most rigorous. Drives V&V process for flight software.

concepts.name: ISO_26262_automotive
concepts.definition: Functional safety of road vehicle electrical/electronic systems. ASIL A-D.
concepts.why: Automotive equivalent of DO-178C. ASIL D (highest risk: brakes, steering) most rigorous. Standard for OEMs + Tier 1.

concepts.name: IEC_61508
concepts.definition: Functional safety of electrical/electronic/programmable electronic safety-related systems. SIL 1-4.
concepts.why: Industrial parent standard. Process industry (refineries, plants). SIL determines required risk reduction.

concepts.name: ASIL_levels
concepts.definition: Automotive Safety Integrity Levels. QM (no requirement) → A → B → C → D. Determined by severity + exposure + controllability.
concepts.why: Drives every architectural decision. ASIL D: full redundancy + extensive analysis. QM: standard quality process. Cost grows with ASIL.

concepts.name: MISRA_C
concepts.definition: C coding standard for safety-critical. Forbid + restrict language features. Static analysis enforced.
concepts.why: Forbids dynamic alloc, recursion, gotos. Avoids undefined behaviour. Automotive + aerospace requirement.

concepts.name: formal_verification_embedded
concepts.definition: Mathematical proof of code correctness. Frama-C, CompCert, seL4.
concepts.why: Highest assurance. seL4 microkernel formally verified. CompCert verified C compiler. Used where bugs cannot exist (medical, aerospace).

concepts.name: triple_modular_redundancy
concepts.definition: TMR: 3 identical units, vote on output. 2-out-of-3 majority.
concepts.why: Hardware fault tolerance. Voter is critical path. SpaceX Dragon (3x flight computers), space (radiation). Cost: 3x hardware.

concepts.name: lockstep_CPUs
concepts.definition: Two CPUs execute same instructions. Outputs compared each cycle. Mismatch = fault.
concepts.why: Hardware fault detection. ARM Cortex-R lockstep. ASIL D requirement. Cost: 2x compute for fault detection.

concepts.name: watchdog_kick_pattern
concepts.definition: Periodic 'I'm alive' signal to watchdog timer. Missing kick = reset.
concepts.why: Last-resort recovery. Different from heartbeat (network): hardware-level. Independent of software state.

concepts.name: diagnostic_trouble_codes
concepts.definition: DTCs: standard error codes. OBD-II in cars. Logged + reported.
concepts.why: Field diagnostics. Mechanic reads DTC → knows issue. Embedded systems log + transmit. Foundation of automotive maintenance.

concepts.name: fail_safe_design
concepts.definition: On failure, system enters known-safe state. Brakes lock open, valves close, robots stop.
concepts.why: Foundation of safety-critical. Failure inevitable; bound consequences. Drives mechanical + control design.

concepts.name: Yocto_embedded_linux
concepts.definition: Build system for custom embedded Linux distros. BitBake recipes + layers.
concepts.why: Reproducible custom Linux. Industrial + commercial embedded. Trade: steep learning curve. Industry standard for embedded Linux.

concepts.name: Buildroot
concepts.definition: Simpler embedded Linux build system. Makefile-based. Faster than Yocto for simpler use cases.
concepts.why: Smaller projects + faster iteration. No layered architecture; rebuild whole config. Easier learning curve.

concepts.name: PREEMPT_RT_Linux
concepts.definition: Kernel patch making Linux preemptible. Bounded latencies (typically tens of µs).
concepts.why: Linux for soft RT + many hard RT. Industrial control, audio production, robotics. Mainlining ongoing; full inclusion expected 2024-2025.

rules.name: hard_RT_requires_worst_case_bounded
if: a system has hard real-time deadlines
then: WCET must be bounded + system designed for worst case
rules.why: Average behaviour irrelevant; worst case = correctness. Caches + branch prediction + DRAM refresh add jitter; must be analysed or eliminated.

rules.name: RMS_optimal_for_fixed_priority
rules.why: Liu + Layland 1973. If RMS can't schedule, no fixed-priority assignment can. Foundation of RT scheduling theory.

rules.name: EDF_optimal_among_all_schedulers
if: a task set has total utilisation ≤ 1
rules.why: Earliest Deadline First: optimal in single-processor preemptive scheduling. Cost: dynamic priorities, harder analysis. RMS easier to analyse + reason about.

rules.name: priority_inheritance_bounds_priority_inversion
then: priority inversion is bounded by critical section duration
rules.why: Without: low-priority task holding mutex blocks high-priority indefinitely. With inheritance: holder runs at high priority until release. Mars Pathfinder fix.

rules.name: static_allocation_required_for_safety_critical
rules.why: malloc: bounded time? Fragmentation? OOM? Cannot prove. Static: all sizes known at compile, no fragmentation possible. MISRA C + DO-178C requirement.

rules.name: interrupt_latency_dominates_response_time
then: interrupt latency is in critical path
rules.why: Time from event to handler: HW + (interrupts disabled) + entry. Cortex-M deterministic entry; disabling interrupts adds. Critical sections matter.

rules.name: DMA_enables_RT_throughput
if: peripheral throughput exceeds CPU per-byte service time
rules.why: CPU servicing every byte: limited throughput. DMA: peripheral ↔ memory autonomously. CPU free for other work. Standard for fast peripherals.

rules.name: MCU_choice_balances_constraints
rules.why: Cortex-M0: cheap, low power. M4F: DSP capability. M7: speed. ESP32: Wi-Fi/BT integrated. RISC-V: no fees. Choice cascades through firmware design.

rules.name: MQTT_for_publish_subscribe_IoT
rules.why: HTTP: per-request overhead, polling-based. MQTT: persistent connection, pub/sub, lighter framing. Standard IoT messaging. AWS IoT Core, Azure IoT Hub.

rules.name: BLE_for_low_power_proximate
if: device communicates with phone or nearby gateway
rules.why: Native phone support. Low power. 10m range typical. Wearables, sensors, beacons. Bluetooth 5+ adds mesh + audio.

rules.name: Matter_unifies_smart_home
rules.why: Apple, Google, Amazon, Samsung all support. Customers expect cross-ecosystem. Trade: complexity + maturity (early days). Industry direction.

rules.name: LoRaWAN_for_long_range_low_data
if: sensors are kilometres apart + send small data infrequently
rules.why: Battery years. Public + private networks (TTN, Helium). Cost: low throughput, latency. Trade-off for asset tracking, agriculture.

rules.name: CAN_for_automotive_robustness
if: robust real-time messaging in noisy electrical environment
rules.why: Differential signalling, prioritised arbitration, fault detection. Decades of automotive deployment. Used in robotics + industrial too.

rules.name: DDS_real_time_publish_subscribe
if: robotic or industrial system needs distributed pub-sub with QoS
rules.why: Strong typing, rich QoS, decentralised discovery. ROS2 foundation. Industrial deployment. Trade: complexity vs MQTT.

rules.name: Kalman_filter_optimal_for_Gaussian_linear
if: state + measurement noise are Gaussian + system is linear
then: Kalman filter is the optimal estimator
rules.why: Mathematically provable optimal. Extended Kalman handles non-linear by linearising. Foundation of sensor fusion.

rules.name: complementary_filter_pragmatic_alternative
if: compute is constrained + Gaussian assumption acceptable
then: complementary filter works almost as well as Kalman
rules.why: Much cheaper. IMU attitude: weighted combination of integrated gyro + accelerometer tilt. Many drones use; good enough.

rules.name: quantization_critical_for_MCU_ML
then: int8 quantization required for practical performance
rules.why: Float emulated = 10-100x slower. Int8 native + fast. Quality loss ~1-2%. CMSIS-NN, TFLite Micro all expect quantized models.

rules.name: watchdog_required_for_unattended_operation
rules.why: Software bugs + hardware glitches happen. Without watchdog: system hangs forever. With: hardware reset = recovery. Universal embedded practice.

rules.name: MISRA_C_required_for_automotive
rules.why: Forbids constructs prone to undefined behaviour + hard to verify. Static analysis enforces. Audited. Standard automotive requirement.

rules.name: TMR_for_radiation_environments
then: Triple Modular Redundancy required for compute
rules.why: Single Event Upsets flip memory bits + corrupt computation. TMR: 3 units vote = majority correct. SpaceX Dragon, JPL spacecraft.

rules.name: lockstep_for_ASIL_D
rules.why: Two CPUs execute identically; voter compares each cycle. Mismatch = fault → safe state. Cortex-R lockstep. Standard for steering, brakes.

rules.name: fail_safe_design_bounds_failure_consequences
rules.why: Without: failure → unknown state. With: failure → defined safe state (motor off, valve closed, brakes locked). Foundation of safety engineering.

rules.name: formal_verification_for_zero_bug_requirements
rules.why: Testing finds bugs; verification proves their absence. seL4 microkernel, CompCert compiler. Cost: 10-50x development effort. Used where justified.
